# Frontend Context Menu

Use only the rules that apply to the current consumer task.

## Contents

- [Accessible context menus](#accessible-context-menus)

## Accessible context menus

Open context menus through NhContextMenuService with text titles, iconClass icons, a keyboard-reachable opener and actions whose failures still close the menu.

## Preferred approach

Inject `NhContextMenuService` and open one menu at a time with
`NhContextMenu.fromEvent(event).withItems([...])` from a `(contextmenu)` handler
that calls `event.preventDefault()`. Give every right-click target a
keyboard-reachable equivalent, such as an actions button with
`aria-haspopup="menu"`, and open the same items there with
`NhContextMenu.fromElement(button)`, which anchors the menu below the button.

Pass translated, user-facing text as `NhContextMenuItem.title`. Titles are
rendered as text, so a project name or another user-entered value is safe in a
title and markup in it is shown literally. Put an icon in `iconClass` (for
example `ph ph-folder-open`); the service renders it as a hidden
`<i aria-hidden="true">` before the title. Use `{type: 'divider'}` for a
separator, `checked: true | false` for a checkbox item and `disabled: true` for
an action the user cannot run now.

Return a promise from `onClick`. The menu stays open until it settles and then
closes, also when it rejects; the rejection goes to Angular's `ErrorHandler`, so
the providers registered through `NH_ERROR_HANDLERS` see it. Show the user a
localized result yourself; the menu does not.

The menu is a WAI-ARIA menu (`role="menu"` with `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`
and `separator` items). Opening it focuses the first item; the arrow keys, Home
and End move, PageUp and PageDown act as Home and End, Enter and Space activate,
and Escape or Tab close it and return focus to the element that had it. A
disabled item stays reachable with the arrow keys but cannot be activated. The
menu is fixed to the viewport, flips left or up near an edge, stays inside the
viewport and scrolls when it is taller than the viewport. It closes on a
pointer down outside it, on Escape, on a scroll of the page or of any inner
container, and on a window resize. Change `config.zIndex` when the menu must
appear above other overlays.

Style `.nh-context-menu`, `.nh-context-menu-item`, `.divider`,
`.nh-context-menu-item-icon`, `.nh-context-menu-item-title`, `[aria-checked]`,
`[aria-disabled="true"]`, `:focus` and `:focus-visible` in the application
theme, or use the default stylesheet shipped in the package's `styles` folder.
Keep a visible focus indicator.

## Avoid

- Putting HTML in `title` for icons or emphasis; use `iconClass`.
- Offering an action only through a right-click.
- Passing page coordinates such as `pageX`/`pageY`, or adding the scroll offset
  yourself: `x` and `y` are viewport coordinates.
- Swallowing errors inside `onClick` to keep the menu open, or leaving the menu
  open until a long-running request finishes when a modal or page should show
  the progress instead.
- Overriding the inline position, size or overflow styles the service sets.

## Verification

Run `npx ng test nh-common --include projects/nh-common/src/lib/services/nh-context-menu.service.spec.ts`
from `src/Front-end`. In the management sample's platform lab, right-click the
project row and open Project actions with Enter: check focus on the first item,
arrow-key movement past the separator, the disabled Archive item, the Pinned
check mark, Escape and Tab returning focus to the button, and the failing
action closing the menu. Type markup into the project code and check that the
menu shows it as text. Check the menu near the right and bottom edges, on a
scrolled page and at a narrow mobile width.
